transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose what really scared me enough to ask for help is that... I keep having these mornings where I think it might just be easier if I didn't wake up. I want to be clear that I don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself, but having those thoughts at all just made me realize I should probably come in and talk to someone.
Have you experienced these feelings of hopelessness before, or is this the first time in your life you have felt this way?

No, this is really the first time. It's... well, it's been going on for about a month now. It started right after my sister passed away. It was very unexpected, and... I just haven't been the same since.
Besides these thoughts of not wanting to wake up, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Well, my appetite has definitely changed. Food just doesn't really call to me much anymore. I'll go to the kitchen and fix a little toast or maybe some soup, and then... well, I'll realize by the evening that I've barely eaten anything all day. I'm certainly not trying to lose weight, I just don't have the desire to eat right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since this started?

Yes, my sleep has definitely been off. I... I tend to fall asleep in bits and pieces now, just sort of dozing. And then I'll wake up before dawn, and my mind is just already turning. Once I'm up like that, I usually can't get settled again before the day actually starts.
Has this recent change in your mood or energy level made it difficult for you to keep up with your responsibilities at work or in your day-to-day life?

Yes, it has. I'm retired, but I stay busy... or I usually do. Lately, I've had to ask another volunteer to cover parts of the Juneteenth budgeting workshop I help run. I just can't keep up with the preparation the way I normally would. And in my day-to-day life, I've been turning down neighbors and friends when they ask to get together, much more than usual. I just don't have the energy for it right now.
Have you noticed if you feel physically restless and unable to sit still, or conversely, that you feel like you are moving and speaking much more slowly than usual?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel restless or fidgety, and... well, I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than normal. I just don't have much energy to do things, like I mentioned, but my actual movements seem about the same as they always are.

Do you feel that your current mood and lack of energy are almost entirely centered around the grief of losing your sister, or do you feel that your sadness and lack of motivation are becoming something more pervasive that exists even when you aren't specifically thinking about her?

I... I'm really not sure how to answer that. It's hard to separate it all out. I mean, I miss her, obviously, but I haven't really paid attention to whether I only feel this way when I'm actively thinking about her. 

It just sort of feels like this heaviness is there in the background most days right now. So I guess... I just don't know if it's entirely about the grief or if it's turned into something else. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Have you noticed any moments over the past few weeks where you felt briefly able to experience pleasure or a temporary lift in your mood, perhaps when you were distracted by something else?

Not really, no. I mean, I still make myself show up for things... like my book club, or the community dance night. But lately, I just sit there feeling like I'm behind a pane of glass. I'm there, but I'm not really taking any of it in. Even the things I usually love, like working in my garden or cooking for the neighbors... they just don't give me that little lift they used to. It's just flat.
